title: Minor Hall's death; Jazzmen errors and Bolden doubts
summary: Russell notes Minor Hall's death, the errors in Jazzmen, and doubts about Bolden's existence and the photograph.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah, no, Minor died. We got a good interview with him in 1958. Wow. He was playing very little then. He had left the Ori band in a disagreement.
I have a record he made with Joe Dierensburg. He might have played a little bit after that, not much.

So, because he, I heard. The LARP record? Yeah. It was made about that time, actually. He had cancer, I heard, at that time. He looked in pretty good health and talked like he'd be playing, like he was alright. But a couple years later, maybe about two years ago, he died. So, evidently he did have cancer. And he was one of the better drummers, not flashy in any way either. And maybe in some sense, monotonous compared to some of the other New Orleans drummers, but still a wonderful rhythm section. Buster Wilson was the other member of that section, which was easily the best I ever heard. Really terrific. So, I'll send some of these and go over the ones that you don't, that I don't have here, like George Bakke and Johnny Dodds notes. I have another interview someplace of Jimmy Noon. We did at that time, too. It's very difficult to get anybody down here that can tell anything about him at all. There's conflicting stories. But I'll send the dope that we got directly from him, which isn't as good as a real interview because it's, it went through me and then through Lee Smith and then done longhand. It's very sketchy. So, I think that finishes up what I had to say about preparing Jazzman, which incidentally has just hundreds and hundreds of errors in. Maybe not, maybe not quite the proportion, let's say a little red back book. By whom? You know, the Sam Charter's book, which has an unusual number of errors and misspellings in, which was done maybe 15 years later. It should have had less maybe, but I'm not trying to make excuses for the Jazzman, which is so far from perfect. We always should have gone back and revised it. But there's just a terrific amount of errors and things in there. Right now, speaking of errors, we still don't know much about Buddy Bolden, for instance. I remember one time speaking of Sam, since he brought in the name, about maybe as long as three years ago, he served notice on me. He said, if you all don't dig up some real documentary dope, we'll call it, on Bolden by the New York people, like Meaden, Marshall Stearns, and all the other New York authors, are just going to cross him off the list as really never having existed. There's no proof that he ever really lived. Who said that? Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. it backwards by the way I might put that in here too because two of the players there it's something we still can't understand the bass players holding his instrument if it's if you turn the negative around two of them have to be you're holding it left-handed we don't know of anybody in the band that's left-handed the way it's printed now the clarinet is left-handed holding it with the hands wrong and the carnet probably isn't holding it naturally but the bass and guitar holding it as if they were right-handed and Jimmy Johnson and Brock were right-handed and yet if you turn the negative around the way it really should be to be right they're going to be holding probably the photographer wanted the bass on a certain side and had it it's hard to understand though that they would have made those two right-handed fellows hold it left-handed but some of them have to be holding it wrong so I mean there's those little things like that that should have been pointed out in Jasmine which we didn't even think about or didn't even see well we didn't know what to think in those days we were ignorant then and still are you know but the clarinet both clarinets have their fingers wrong so they wouldn't be holding that way but these fellows are holding it right according to being right-handed the bass and the guitar but it must have been shifted around probably also the it's hard to say how Bowen would have been holding that horn it looks like it's wrong too from where the mouthpiece is it's so dim it's hard to say but the point I was going to make is that this simply has to be Bolden these people we do have pictures of Cornish other places and Jimmy Johnson who looked like though they do their photo came from Cornish yes that's what I say Charles Smith got it so I mean of course some of the New York writers would say we don't have anything to document that Bolden never lived he is listed in the the big swords directory from 1901 to 1905 I noticed
